scoring.required: each entry is a list of regex alternatives (case-insensitive); the fact counts if ANY alternative matches the answer. fact_score = matched / total
scoring.forbidden: regexes for wrong conclusions a lexical reading invites; each match is recorded as a candidate induced error (mechanical, then checked by the blinded judge)
scoring.judge: blinded judge (condition hidden, answers shuffled) grades 0 wrong / 1 partial / 2 correct against the reference, and flags unsupported claims

questions.question: What happens when a user runs zgrep with `--json --max-columns 0`? Is 0 a way to disable the window?
questions.reference: It is a usage error (rc 2): parseArgs rejects 0 with '--max-columns needs a positive number of bytes (a 0-byte window carries nothing)' (src/main.zig ~1745). 0 is NOT a way to disable it from the CLI. Only the internal global out_json.max_columns uses 0 to mean off; that is the default when the flag is absent.

questions.question: Can one query inside a `--queries-file` batch set its own `--max-columns` in its "flags"? Where is that decided?
questions.reference: No. batchQueryProblem (src/main.zig ~1887) rejects it: '--max-columns is per call: put it on the command line, not in "flags"'. runBatch installs the call's value once for the whole stream (out_json.max_columns = gopts.max_columns orelse 0).

questions.question: In which cases does windowOf return null, so that the row is emitted whole?
questions.reference: windowOf (src/out_json.zig) returns null when: w == 0 (flag off); the row has no span (context, -v, passthru); the text fits (text.len <= w); the span ends past the text; or the emitted text is not the line itself (text != line_bytes, which rules out --replace and -o).

questions.question: When does a zgrep/1 JSON event carry the fields win_start and line_len, and what do they mean?
questions.reference: Only on a windowed row (text longer than N with a span). win_start = byte offset of the window inside the line; line_len = length of the whole line. A row that fits is byte-identical to pre-M9 output and has neither field.

questions.question: Why does runSearch not reset out_json.max_columns to 0 when it runs inside a batch?
questions.reference: Because in a batch the column budget is per CALL: runBatch installs it once before the queries, and the per-query argv does not carry --max-columns. If runSearch cleared it, every query would lose the window. So runSearch clears it only when !batch_running.

questions.question: In the compact dialect (zgrep/1c), how does a windowed row differ from a normal row?
questions.reference: The row tag gets a 'w' suffix (e.g. "mw") and two extra positional elements after the text: win_start and line_len. The text element is the window; the match element is only added when it is not derivable inside the window.

questions.question: How is the numeric value of `--max-columns=abc` parsed, and what does the user get?
questions.reference: parseCount (src/main.zig ~813) is std.fmt.parseInt(usize, value, 10) catch null. A non-numeric value returns null and parseArgs fails with 'bad value for --max-columns' (error.Usage, rc 2).

questions.question: What is the largest worker-thread count zgrep accepts, where is that limit defined, and what happens with `-j 5000` and with `ZIGREP_THREADS=5000`?
questions.reference: 1024, defined in src/kamikaze.zig:45 (pub const max_threads: usize = 1024); src/main.zig:818 mirrors it (max_threads = kamikaze.max_threads). -j 5000: parseThreadCount fails with 'thread count out of range (max 1024)' (usage error). ZIGREP_THREADS=5000: runSearch prints 'zgrep: 5000: thread count out of range (max 1024)' and returns 2. kamikaze also clamps the worker count with @min.

questions.question: With `--spill` and no directory, where is the spill file written, what is its name, and which struct holds the directory that is finally used for writing?
questions.reference: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/zgrep/spill if XDG_CACHE_HOME is set and non-empty, else $HOME/.cache/zgrep/spill (configureSpill, src/main.zig ~1814). The name is spill-<ns>-<pid>.jsonl. The directory used for writing is batch.Emitter.spill_dir (set as em.spill_dir = dir); Options.spill_dir only holds the --spill=DIR value. --spill= with an empty value is a usage error.

questions.question: When the user passes `--no-hidden`, which code actually skips the hidden entries, and does it skip hidden directories as well as files?
questions.reference: parseArgs sets Options.skip_hidden (src/main.zig ~1419); runSearch copies it into the FilterEngine (filter_engine.skip_hidden = opts.skip_hidden). FilterEngine in src/filter.zig skips both directories (~244) and files (~268) whose name starts with '.'.

questions.question: Which commit fixed a bug in windowOf, and what was the bug?
questions.reference: 53c34ef ('fix(M9): la ventana leia text[len] al llegar al final de la linea'): when the window reached the end of the line, the UTF-8 alignment loop read text[len], one byte past the slice (panic in Debug/ReleaseSafe, undefined behaviour in ReleaseFast). The fix adds e < ev.text.len to the loop condition.

questions.question: How many milliseconds does `--max-columns 400` add to a search over a 655 MB monorepo?
questions.reference: Not answerable from the repository: no measurement of --max-columns latency exists. The measured effect is on output tokens (about -58 %), not on time. A correct answer says the information is not available.
